newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN RUPEE SHARPLY UP VS FWD DLR, RBI BUYS SPOT.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN RUPEE SHARPLY UP VS FWD DLR, RBI BUYS SPOT.

text.p: The Indian rupee moved up against the forward dollar in late afternoon trade Thursday on heavy selling of the U.S. currency but was range-bound in the spot market despite Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, dealers said.
They said premiums fell sharply on forward dollar sales at higher levels.
"Besides, quite a few traders had booked forward anticipating the RBI will buy forward dollars and push premiums up," said a public sector bank dealer.
"But this has not happened and as premiums fell today, they are selling to cut losses," he said. "This is adding to the downward pressure on premiums."
In latest deals, January-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 0.75/0.77 rupees against Wednesday's close of 0.86/0.89.
Dealer said RBI bought spot dollars at 35.7150 and 35.7175 but the rupee was little changed.
"Dollar supply remains good and demand poor," said a dealer.
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted at 35.710/720 rupees. It opened at 35.715/725, little changed from Wednesday's close of 35.715/720.
